keys.fashionCatalog.editor.provenOptions: {count} options are proven by the loaded source set.

keys.flagworkSave.viewerHelp: A read only map from Sword and Shield Flagwork hash table entries to their derived save keys, with source provenance and optional configured save metadata. This viewer never changes game files or the save.
keys.flagworkSave.low32Help: The lower 32 bits of this entry's 64 bit hash, formatted as an eight digit hexadecimal value. Flagwork uses this derived value as the save key. Different full hashes can share one Low32 key; diagnostics report detected collisions.
keys.flagworkSave.valueKindHelp: How the saved value is interpreted. Flag entries are boolean true or false values. Work entries are integers. KM derives this classification from the table and entry naming convention; this viewer is read only.
keys.hyperTraining.minimumLevelHelp: The lowest Pokemon level accepted by Hyper Training. Applying a change synchronizes the script eligibility check, party and box picker checks, and available English dialogue. The vanilla minimum is level 100.
keys.hyperTraining.cutoffHelp: The exact whole number threshold to stage, from 1 through 100. Pokemon at or above this level qualify for Hyper Training; Pokemon below it do not.
keys.fieldHelp.catalog.generic.selection: Selects the stored value used by this field. Choose a listed option unless you are intentionally preserving an existing raw value
keys.fieldHelp.catalog.generic.value: Edits the value stored for this field. Preserve unfamiliar raw values unless their behavior has been verified
keys.fieldHelp.catalog.domain.items: Controls an item-data property used when the game loads or processes this item
keys.fieldHelp.catalog.domain.pokemon: Controls a species or form property in the personal Pokemon data
keys.fieldHelp.catalog.domain.moves: Controls a move property read by the game's battle logic
keys.fieldHelp.catalog.domain.trainers: Controls a trainer, battle, or party setting for this trainer entry
keys.fieldHelp.catalog.domain.pokemonInstance: Controls how this particular Pokemon instance is created. It does not edit the species globally
keys.fieldHelp.catalog.domain.encounters: Controls how this encounter or spawner entry selects and creates Pokemon
keys.fieldHelp.catalog.domain.raids: Controls a Pokemon or probability value for this raid entry
keys.fieldHelp.catalog.domain.raidRewards: Controls a reward item or quantity for this raid reward row
keys.fieldHelp.catalog.domain.shops: Controls an inventory or unlock value for this shop row
keys.fieldHelp.catalog.domain.behavior: Controls an AI behavior value. Preserve values whose effect has not been verified in game
keys.fieldHelp.catalog.domain.placement: Controls a property of this placed world object. Changes affect this instance, not every object of the same type
keys.fieldHelp.catalog.reference.species: Selects the Pokemon species referenced by this record. Changing species may change which forms, abilities, or other dependent choices are valid
keys.fieldHelp.catalog.reference.form: Selects the species form. Form numbers are species-specific; Base is normally 0, and unavailable forms should not be forced
keys.fieldHelp.catalog.reference.item: Selects the referenced item. None removes the item where that is supported
keys.fieldHelp.catalog.reference.move: Selects the move stored in this move slot. None uses the record's supported empty or default behavior
keys.fieldHelp.catalog.reference.move.za: Selects the move stored in this slot. Game default / auto (0) asks the game to generate moves using its normal rules. None (-1) deliberately leaves the slot empty. These values are not interchangeable
keys.fieldHelp.catalog.pokemon.level: Sets the level used when this Pokemon instance is created
keys.fieldHelp.catalog.pokemon.trait: Selects an authored Pokemon trait for this record. Random or default modes defer the final choice to the game
keys.fieldHelp.catalog.pokemon.shiny: Controls whether shiny appearance is fixed, forbidden, or left to the game's normal roll, depending on the available modes
keys.fieldHelp.catalog.pokemon.statValue: Controls a stored stat, IV, EV, yield, or stat preset. Its exact role is identified by the field label
keys.fieldHelp.catalog.pokemon.specialMechani: Controls a game-specific Pokemon mechanic such as Dynamax, Gigantamax, Tera type, Alpha behavior, or size. It has no effect where the surrounding record cannot use that mechanic
keys.fieldHelp.catalog.pokemon.type: Selects one of the species' stored types. The second type may match the first for a single-type Pokemon
keys.fieldHelp.catalog.pokemon.progression: Controls a stored progression value such as experience yield, growth, friendship, catch rate, or evolution stage
keys.fieldHelp.catalog.pokemon.breeding: Controls a stored breeding property such as egg group or hatch cycles
keys.fieldHelp.catalog.pokemon.learnsetMove: Selects the move learned when this level-up learnset row's requirement is met
keys.fieldHelp.catalog.pokemon.learnsetLevel: Sets the level requirement stored for this level-up learnset row. Special labels such as Evolution are preserved where the game supports them
keys.fieldHelp.catalog.pokemon.compatibility: The group selects a TM, TR, or tutor-move list; each toggle controls whether this species and form can learn that move from the selected source. It does not add the move to the level-up learnset
keys.fieldHelp.catalog.pokemon.evolutionMetho: Selects the trigger the game checks for this evolution row. The selected method determines how the argument and level fields are interpreted
keys.fieldHelp.catalog.pokemon.evolutionArgum: Stores the method-specific parameter for this evolution row, such as an item, condition, or other requirement. Interpret it together with Evolution method
keys.fieldHelp.catalog.pokemon.evolutionTarge: Selects the species produced when this evolution row succeeds
Selects the target species form produced by this evolution row. Form numbers are specific to the target species
keys.fieldHelp.catalog.pokemon.evolutionLevel: Sets the level requirement used by evolution methods that check a level. Methods without a level requirement may ignore it
keys.fieldHelp.catalog.pokemon.alphaMove: Selects the move granted to Alpha instances of this exact species and form by Z-A's Alpha move table. It is separate from the normal level-up moveset
keys.fieldHelp.catalog.pokemon.dexDestination: Selects the Regular or Hyperspace Pokédex destination when moving this Z-A species. The destination slot chooses its exact displayed position and the move updates the Pokédex boundary counts
keys.fieldHelp.catalog.item.price: Sets the stored purchase price in the currency represented by this field. Shop rows can override item-table prices in games that store prices per inventory slot
keys.fieldHelp.catalog.item.sellPrice: Sets the item's stored sell value. The game may apply its own shop rules when displaying or paying this amount
keys.fieldHelp.catalog.item.category: Selects the item's stored pocket, category, or type used for organization and behavior routing
keys.fieldHelp.catalog.item.sortOrder: Controls where the item is ordered inside its applicable list or pocket. It does not change the item's effect
keys.fieldHelp.catalog.item.machine: Links this item to its TM or machine move and, where present, its displayed machine number
keys.fieldHelp.catalog.item.battleUse: Controls where the item may be selected or used. This classification does not create a missing effect handler
keys.fieldHelp.catalog.item.statusCure: Stores which status conditions this item cures. Use named controls where available so unrelated bits remain unchanged
keys.fieldHelp.catalog.item.useFlags: Raw item-use flags decoded by the editor where their meaning is known. Preserve unknown bits
keys.fieldHelp.catalog.item.maxUseLevel: Highest target level accepted by this item's use handler. It is not an evolution requirement and does not combine a direct Use Item evolution with a level gate
keys.fieldHelp.catalog.item.flingPower: Base power used when this item is consumed by Fling or the game's equivalent thrown-item mechanic. It does not change the item's normal use effect
keys.fieldHelp.catalog.item.ppGain: Amount of PP restored by this item's use handler. It is not the move's maximum PP or the number of times the item can be used
keys.fieldHelp.catalog.move.core: Controls a core move property such as type, damage class, or PP. Battle behavior can also depend on the move's effect handler
keys.fieldHelp.catalog.move.power: Sets the move's base power value. A value of 0 is commonly used for status moves or moves whose damage is calculated by special logic
keys.fieldHelp.catalog.move.healingFlag: Marks this move as a healing move for battle rules and interactions. It does not set how much HP is restored; recovery amounts come from separate fields or effect logic
keys.fieldHelp.catalog.move.accuracy: Sets the move's stored hit chance. Special effect handlers may apply additional targeting or hit rules
keys.fieldHelp.catalog.move.priority: Controls when the move is chosen relative to moves at other priority levels; normal speed ordering still applies between equal priorities
keys.fieldHelp.catalog.move.condition: Selects the conventional condition or secondary effect associated with the move
keys.fieldHelp.catalog.move.effectChance: Sets the chance for the associated secondary effect or stat change. In tables that use 0 for a primary effect, 0 means no separate chance roll
keys.fieldHelp.catalog.move.duration: Controls the stored duration or duration mode for the associated effect. Zero may mean effect-defined where the field supports that convention
keys.fieldHelp.catalog.move.recovery: Controls HP recovery, draining, recoil, or another signed healing parameter. The field label and effect handler determine the exact direction
keys.fieldHelp.catalog.move.statChange: Configures one stat-change slot: which stat changes, by how many stages, or with what chance
keys.fieldHelp.catalog.move.critical: Selects the stored critical-hit rank used by this move's runtime battle data
keys.fieldHelp.catalog.move.enabled: Controls whether this move is enabled. Enabling a base-disabled move does not restore missing animations, resources, or references
keys.fieldHelp.catalog.move.behavior: Selects the verified Z-A runtime behavior category. It also determines how related runtime effect and stat fields are interpreted
keys.fieldHelp.catalog.move.runtimeCondition: Controls the separate Z-A runtime-condition channel. It is independent from the conventional move condition fields
keys.fieldHelp.catalog.move.specialConditionF: Special runtime flag whose general meaning is not verified. It is not the master switch for runtime conditions; most condition-bearing moves leave it disabled
keys.fieldHelp.catalog.move.rawEffect: Advanced effect parameter interpreted by the move's effect handler. Preserve it unless this move's behavior has been verified
keys.fieldHelp.catalog.move.flinch: Chance for conventional Flinch. In Z-A, Flinch can cancel a move during wind-up and put that move on cooldown; it is separate from Damage reaction chance
keys.fieldHelp.catalog.move.damageReaction: Chance that an eligible hit forces the target to play its standard damage-recoil animation. 100 means every eligible hit reacts. This does not scale the animation duration, delay the target's next move, or apply conventional Flinch's cooldown
keys.fieldHelp.catalog.move.cooldown: Sets the Z-A cooldown in seconds before the move can be used again. This is independent from Damage reaction chance
keys.fieldHelp.catalog.move.timing: Controls a verified Z-A runtime timing value. The field label identifies which event or offset it affects
keys.fieldHelp.catalog.move.projectile: Controls projectile count or the verified locator from which the move effect is spawned
keys.fieldHelp.catalog.move.range: Sets a boundary of the move's targeting range. The minimum must not exceed the maximum
keys.fieldHelp.catalog.trainer.identity: Selects the trainer class or class-linked presentation data used by this trainer record
keys.fieldHelp.catalog.trainer.battleSetup: Controls a trainer-level battle setup value such as battle type or rank
keys.fieldHelp.catalog.trainer.ai: Stores battle AI flags. Use named flag controls when available so unrelated bits remain unchanged
keys.fieldHelp.catalog.trainer.money: Stores the game-specific trainer money rate rather than a final payout amount
keys.fieldHelp.catalog.trainer.money.swsh: Stores the raw Sword and Shield trainer money rate. Its exact payout behavior has not been verified, so KM does not present it as a final cash amount
keys.fieldHelp.catalog.trainer.money.sv: Stores the signed Scarlet and Violet trainer money rate. KM exposes the raw rate because its exact payout behavior has not been verified
keys.fieldHelp.catalog.trainer.money.za: Stores the Z-A trainer money rate as an unsigned value from 0 to 255. Base prize money is the highest party level x this rate x 4; separate player bonuses can increase the final reward
keys.fieldHelp.catalog.trainer.specialMechani: Enables a game-specific trainer battle mechanic. A compatible party Pokemon and valid battle context may still be required
keys.fieldHelp.catalog.trainer.lastHand: Makes the Pokemon in the final party slot come out last, overriding ordinary send-out preferences such as Mega Evolution. It does not automatically choose the strongest Pokemon
keys.fieldHelp.catalog.trade.requirement: Controls which Pokemon or trait the player must offer for this in-game trade
keys.fieldHelp.catalog.trade.provenance: Controls stored Original Trainer or provenance data on the Pokemon received from this trade
keys.fieldHelp.catalog.adventure.rule: Controls a Dynamax Adventure encounter or capture rule for this record
keys.fieldHelp.catalog.staticEncounter.scenar: Selects the authored scenario or presentation used when this static encounter starts. Preserve unknown scenarios unless tested
keys.fieldHelp.catalog.encounter.probability: Sets this slot's direct encounter probability within the table's probability model
keys.fieldHelp.catalog.encounter.weight: Sets this slot's relative selection weight. Its actual percentage depends on the total weight of all eligible slots
keys.fieldHelp.catalog.encounter.level: Sets a minimum, maximum, or fixed level used when the encounter creates a Pokemon
keys.fieldHelp.catalog.encounter.population: Controls how many Pokemon this slot or spawner may create. Related minimum and maximum fields must remain consistent
keys.fieldHelp.catalog.encounter.strength: Sets a Z-A encounter strengthening value for the named stat. This is separate from ordinary IVs
keys.fieldHelp.catalog.raid.probability: Sets this raid entry's selection probability for the star tier named by the field
keys.fieldHelp.catalog.raid.setup: Controls raid eligibility or grouping, such as game version, difficulty tier, or delivery group. It does not change the Pokemon's species data
keys.fieldHelp.catalog.raid.bossRule: Controls a raid boss HP multiplier, shield threshold, or double-action threshold and rate. Disabled or default sentinel values remain game-defined where offered
keys.fieldHelp.catalog.raid.reward: Sets the reward value or quantity for the star tier named by the field
keys.fieldHelp.catalog.shop.inventory: Controls the item or inventory assignment for this shop slot
keys.fieldHelp.catalog.shop.unlock: Controls when this shop slot becomes available. The condition kind determines how its comparison and arguments are interpreted
keys.fieldHelp.catalog.behavior.mode: Selects the AI behavior profile used by this entry. The profile determines how its other behavior parameters are interpreted
keys.fieldHelp.catalog.placement.transform: Controls this object's world position, rotation, or scale on the named axis
keys.fieldHelp.catalog.probability: Sets the stored chance as a percentage or probability value for this field
keys.fieldHelp.catalog.count: Sets the stored number of entries, results, or objects represented by this field
keys.fieldHelp.catalog.raw.unverified: Raw game value whose gameplay meaning has not been verified. It is shown for preservation and diagnosis and should normally be left unchanged
keys.workflowPanels.outputPlanHelp: Previews every file this edit session intends to create or replace, including the source layer used for each file. A plan marked Needs fixes cannot be applied until its blocking diagnostics are resolved.
keys.workflowPanels.diagnosticsHelp: Lists validation and operation messages from the workflow, staged plan, and latest apply attempt. Errors block the affected operation. Warnings call out risks or incomplete support. Information records useful details.
keys.workflowPanels.metric.applyStatusHelp: Summarizes the latest apply attempt: Written when files were produced, No changes when nothing needed writing, Warning when output completed with cautions, or Error when it failed.
keys.workflowPanels.metric.writtenFilesHelp: The number of files actually written by the latest apply attempt. The file list below shows their output paths.
keys.workflowPanels.metric.planStatusHelp: Ready means the current plan passed its blocking validation and can be applied. Needs fixes means at least one error must be resolved before files can be written.
keys.workflowPanels.metric.targetFilesHelp: The number of output files this reviewed plan would create or replace. It is not a count of individual field edits.
keys.advancedWorkflows.reservedRegionsHelp: The number of exact executable byte ranges reserved for this feature. KM uses these boundaries to detect conflicts and avoid changing unrelated ExeFS edits when the feature is updated or removed.
keys.workflows.listHelp: Only workflows supported by the selected game are listed. Availability is based on validated project paths, required source data, and whether the workflow supports editing or viewing for that game.
keys.workflows.searchHelp: Filters this list by workflow name, description, or internal workflow ID. Searching does not change project data or which workflows are available.
keys.workflows.availability.editableHelp: This workflow can read the selected project data and stage changes. Opening it does not write files; writing happens only through Review and Apply.
keys.workflows.availability.viewOnlyHelp: This workflow can inspect the selected project's data, but it does not offer staged edits for this game or project configuration.
keys.workflows.availability.disabledHelp: This workflow cannot open with the current project validation or data support. The visible reason under its description tells you what must be fixed or supplied.
keys.editorSession.lifecycleHelp: Start Editing enables the change controls for a temporary edit session. Staging collects changes for review. Review and Apply validates the planned target files, and files are written only when Apply is confirmed.
keys.projectPaths.help.baseRomFs: The clean extracted RomFS for the selected game. KM Editor reads game data from this folder and never writes to it. Do not select an installed mod or Output Root.
keys.projectPaths.help.baseExeFs: The clean extracted ExeFS for the selected game. KM Editor verifies the selected game and reads executable data from this source. It is never modified.
keys.projectPaths.help.outputRoot: The separate LayeredFS destination and existing mod layer. Existing output is treated as the effective value so later edits preserve prior work. This path must not overlap either clean base folder.
keys.projectPaths.help.saveFile: Optional save used only by save-aware tools. Ordinary RomFS and ExeFS editors do not require it. A tool that writes a save edits this file directly, so keep your own backup.
keys.projectPaths.help.supportFolder: Select the folder containing oo2core_8_win64.dll. KM Editor uses this library to decompress and rebuild the game data used by these editors, but never modifies the DLL.
keys.projectPaths.help.statuses: Not checked means validation has not run. Valid means the path exists and passed its checks. Not set means no path is configured. Missing means the configured path or a required file is absent. Wrong kind means a file was selected where a folder is required, or the reverse. Unsafe means the path overlaps protected input data or belongs to another game.
keys.projectPaths.help.titleId: Title ID used to verify that Base ExeFS and a title-ID-named Output Root belong to the selected game.
keys.health.summaryHelp: Summarizes whether this project can safely open read-only and editable workflows. Path validation and pending edit state are combined here; individual diagnostics below provide the exact reason for a problem.
keys.health.stateHelp: Overall project state after validating the configured paths and required support files.
keys.health.readOnlyHelp: Read-only workflows require valid clean source data but do not need a writable Output Root.
keys.health.writeHelp: Write workflows also require a valid separate Output Root so source data cannot be overwritten.
keys.health.pendingHelp: Changes staged in the current edit session. They remain in memory until Review and Apply writes the approved output plan.
keys.The clean extracted RomFS for the select: The clean extracted RomFS for the selected game. KM Editor reads game data from this folder and never writes to it. Do not select an installed mod or Output Root.
keys.The clean extracted ExeFS for the select: The clean extracted ExeFS for the selected game. KM Editor verifies the selected game and reads executable data from this source. It is never modified.
keys.The separate LayeredFS destination and e: The separate LayeredFS destination and existing mod layer. Existing output is treated as the effective value so later edits preserve prior work. This path must not overlap either clean base folder.
keys.Optional save used only by save-aware to: Optional save used only by save-aware tools. Ordinary RomFS and ExeFS editors do not require it. A tool that writes a save edits this file directly, so keep your own backup.
keys.Select the folder containing oo2core_8_w: Select the folder containing oo2core_8_win64.dll. KM Editor uses this library to decompress and rebuild the game data used by these editors, but never modifies the DLL.
keys.A handler-specific effect parameter whos: A handler-specific effect parameter whose meaning varies by item. Preserve it unless that item effect has been verified.
keys.Used only after a damaging hit that the: Used only after a damaging hit that the target survives and when the move's native flinch chance is zero. It does not add to, replace, or multiply a nonzero native chance.
keys.gameDump.language.label: Text export languages
keys.gameDump.language.help: Export one language or the complete language set. This is independent of KM Editor's display language.
keys.gameDump.confirm.replaceOwned: KM Editor overwrites the exact output paths for selected categories, removes their stale trusted KM-owned formats, and updates the manifest. A trusted dump for another game is replaced as a whole. Other files are preserved.
keys.workflowHelp.npcItemGift.item: Select the item written to this gift slot. Search by item ID or name; unavailable entries stay visible but cannot be selected.
keys.workflowHelp.npcItemGift.amount: Number of copies granted by this gift. Editable normal-item gifts accept 1 to 999. Fixed gifts cannot change quantity, and known key items are always forced to 1.
keys.workflowHelp.gameDump.destination: Folder where KM Editor writes the selected exported data. It is remembered separately for each game and is not the project's Output Root.
keys.workflowHelp.gameDump.format: File format used for this category's exported records. Available formats depend on the category.
keys.workflowHelp.shinyRate.customOdds: Enter the denominator for the desired approximate odds. KM Editor converts it to the nearest supported number of independent 1-in-4096 shiny rolls and shows the actual result before staging.
keys.workflowHelp.typeChart.cells: Each cell controls the damage multiplier used when the row's attacking type hits the column's defending type: Immune (0x), Not Very Effective (0.5x), Normal (1x), or Super Effective (2x).
keys.workflowHelp.fairyGym.outcome: Sets the stat boost, stat drop, or no-effect result applied when this answer is chosen during the Fairy Gym quiz.
keys.dumpImporter.previewReplacement: A successful preview replaces the previous Dump Importer price batch. Unrelated pending edits stay in place; an accepted import for the same stored price field becomes that field's pending edit.
keys.dumpImporter.sourceHelp: Choose a CSV, TSV, or JSON file that matches the loaded import profile. Preview parses and validates its rows, then stages accepted edits in the current session; it does not write output files or alter the source file.
keys.dumpImporter.progressHelp: Source means a file is selected. Preview means it was parsed and validated. Changes means at least one accepted row is staged for later Review and Apply.
keys.dumpImporter.acceptedHelp: Rows whose required identifiers and editable values were valid. Accepted values become staged edits; rejected rows do not change data.
keys.dumpImporter.importedHelp: Accepted field changes currently staged by Dump Importer. They remain in memory until the normal Review and Apply process writes output.
keys.Verified profile-specific battle-stage a: Verified profile-specific battle-stage and HP-phase schedules, controller actions, selectors, move variants, runtime availability, and editability.
keys.Every editable message line for the sele: Every editable message line for the selected game-text language or all available game-text languages, including semantic message keys and source details.
keys.text.language.label: Game language
keys.text.language.help: Selects which localized in-game text files KM loads and edits. This changes the game text language being edited, not KM Editor's interface language.
keys.text.search.placeholder: Search text, message key, or file
keys.text.categories.help: Filters the loaded files and entries to one related part of the game. The rest of this explanation describes the currently selected category.
keys.text.controls.guide.title: Text control reference
keys.text.controls.guide.help: Line breaks are shown as real lines while editing; KM Editor preserves the game's canonical line-break control when the value is staged.
keys.text.controls.length: {count} / {maximum} canonical characters. Text controls count toward this limit.
keys.text.controls.lineBreak.label: Line break
keys.text.controls.lineBreak.insertHelp: Insert a normal line break inside the same message box.
keys.text.controls.lineBreak.description: Starts a new line in the same message box. It is displayed as a real line break while editing.
keys.text.controls.tab.label: Tab spacing
keys.text.controls.tab.insertHelp: Insert the horizontal tab spacing stored by the game.
keys.text.controls.tab.description: Preserves a horizontal tab used for alignment or spacing.
keys.text.controls.waitClear.label: Continue + clear
keys.text.controls.waitClear.insertHelp: Insert the continue-and-clear control. Add a line break separately when needed.
keys.text.controls.waitClear.description: Waits for confirmation and clears the message box before text continues.
keys.text.controls.waitScroll.label: Continue + scroll
keys.text.controls.waitScroll.insertHelp: Insert the continue-and-scroll control. Add a line break separately when needed.
keys.text.controls.waitScroll.description: Waits for confirmation and scrolls the message box before text continues.
keys.text.controls.timedWait.label: Timed pause
keys.text.controls.timedWait.description: Pauses text for the stored numeric duration.
keys.text.controls.indexedBlank.label: Indexed empty line
keys.text.controls.indexedBlank.description: Represents an intentionally empty message line. In verified Z-A text, n is that source file's zero-based line index; preserve it unless replacing the line with visible text.
keys.text.controls.ruby.label: Pronunciation guide
keys.text.controls.ruby.description: Displays ruby/furigana pronunciation above its base text. A third part preserves an alternate base copy; inside pronunciation text, \| and \} escape literal delimiters.

keys.za.trainers.sharedRival.title: Shared Urbain/Taunie Team
keys.za.trainers.sharedRival.selection: This internal trainer row supplies one team to both rivals. The player's saved appearance selects the active rival: a male player faces Taunie, while a female player faces Urbain.
keys.za.trainers.sharedRival.starterBranch: The {branch} starter path comes from this row's internal suffix. That branch does not select the rival or Meowstic's sex.
keys.za.trainers.sharedRival.editScope: Any party edits here affect this shared row, so they apply regardless of which rival the save selects.
keys.za.trainers.sharedRival.meowstic: Vanilla stores Meowstic as form 0 with Trainer-dependent gender. Form 0 is only a stored placeholder here. At runtime, Meowstic matches the active rival: a male player faces Taunie and gets Taunie's female Meowstic; a female player faces Urbain and gets Urbain's male Meowstic. Party slot does not control this. Choosing Male or Female disables trainer-dependent selection and applies the explicit gender and matching stored form to both rival scenarios.
keys.za.trainers.sharedRival.meowstic.details: Trainer-dependent follows the active rival. A male player faces Taunie, so Meowstic resolves to female form 1. A female player faces Urbain, so Meowstic resolves to male form 0. The stored form is only a placeholder, and party slot does not affect this.
keys.za.trainers.sharedRival.meowsticAvailabi: In vanilla, Meowstic first appears in the Mission 8 boss team at Lv. 55 in party slot 3. Later shared rival rows place it in slot 1; earlier rows do not include it.
keys.za.trainers.sharedRival.meowsticAbsent: This vanilla row has no Meowstic. If you add Meowstic in any party slot, runtime rival selection still applies while Gender is Trainer-dependent.
keys.za.trainers.meowstic.defaultGenderOption: Trainer-dependent (male trainer: male / female trainer: female)
keys.za.trainers.meowstic.defaultFormOption: Dynamic (male trainer: male / female trainer: female)
keys.za.trainers.meowstic.formRuntimeSelected: The stored form is ignored while Gender follows the active trainer.
keys.za.trainers.meowstic.detailsDynamic: Trainer-dependent follows the active trainer actor: a male trainer gets the male form and a female trainer gets the female form. The stored form is only a placeholder. Party slot does not affect this.
keys.za.trainers.meowstic.detailsExplicit: An explicit gender disables trainer-dependent selection. The game uses the stored form exactly, so KM Editor limits Form to values that match the selected gender.

keys.moves.runtimeVariant.label: Variant
keys.moves.runtimeVariant.draftRetention: Drafts are retained while variants and timing rows change. Stage submits every valid draft for this move together.
keys.moves.flinch.help: Conventional Flinch is the probability battle logic rolls. Damage reaction chance only controls the separate damage-recoil animation. A held item's configured added-Flinch value, 10% for an unmodified King's Rock, is used only when native Flinch is zero and never stacks with a nonzero native value.
keys.moves.flinch.zaHelp: In Z-A, conventional Flinch is stored once for the base move, outside the Normal, Plus, and Boss runtime variants. Changing it affects every Pokemon and scripted controller that uses this move in any of those variants; the Runtime Variant selector does not scope it. Damage reaction chance controls only the separate damage-recoil animation. A held item's configured added-Flinch value, 10% for an unmodified King's Rock, is used only when native Flinch is zero and never stacks with a nonzero native value.
keys.moves.runtimeBattle.scopeHelp: Every field in this group belongs to the selected runtime variant. It affects every timing profile and every user of that exact move variant, but it does not change the other runtime variants.
keys.moves.runtimeBehavior.help: Choose a verified behavior category. It controls how runtime effects are interpreted and derives the stat recipient shown below. Categories 9 and 10 are unused in verified data and are unavailable.
keys.moves.runtimeEffects.help: Runtime conditions and Damage reaction chance are separate from conventional move effects. Damage reaction chance only rolls the target's standard damage-recoil animation; it does not delay the next move or apply Flinch cooldown. Existing authored duration tuples are preserved; zero values can be move-specific.
keys.moves.statRecipient.label: Stat recipient
keys.moves.statRecipient.help: Derived from Move behavior and the read-only conventional target; this is not a separate writable field.
keys.moves.fieldHelp.flinch: The conventional Flinch probability read by battle logic. It is independent of Damage reaction chance, which only controls the target's standard damage-recoil animation. When this value is zero, battle logic may use a held item's configured added-Flinch value, 10% for an unmodified King's Rock; it does not stack with a nonzero native value.
keys.moves.fieldHelp.flinch.za: In Z-A, this value is stored once for the base move, outside the Normal, Plus, and Boss runtime variants. Changing it affects every use of this move in all three variants, regardless of the selected Runtime Variant. This is the conventional Flinch probability read by battle logic. It is independent of Damage reaction chance, which only controls the target's standard damage-recoil animation. When this value is zero, battle logic may use a held item's configured added-Flinch value, 10% for an unmodified King's Rock; it does not stack with a nonzero native value.
keys.moves.fieldHelp.behavior: Selects the verified runtime move behavior and determines how the stat recipient is derived.
keys.moves.fieldHelp.shrink: Chance that an eligible hit forces the target to play its standard damage-recoil animation. This value belongs only to the selected runtime variant and does not change the other variants. 100 means every eligible hit reacts. This does not scale the animation duration, delay the target's next move, or apply conventional Flinch's cooldown.
keys.moves.fieldHelp.timingAccuracy: Runtime hit chance for the exact Timing Profile selected above. It applies to every timing-row occurrence in that profile, but not to another timing profile or runtime variant. Additional targeting or hit rules can still apply.
keys.moves.fieldHelp.timingCooldown: Cooldown, in seconds, for the exact Timing Profile selected above. It applies to every timing-row occurrence in that profile, but not to another timing profile or runtime variant. It is independent of Flinch and Damage reaction chance.
keys.moves.fieldHelp.runtimeCondition: Contains every condition ID verified in the runtime battle table. This is separate from the conventional move condition list.
keys.moves.fieldHelp.conditionMode: Controls how runtime condition duration is handled. Preserve authored values when a move uses effect-specific timing.
keys.moves.fieldHelp.specialConditionFlag: Special runtime flag with no verified general-purpose meaning. It is not the master switch for runtime conditions.

keys.moves.runtimeStatus.timingOnly: Exact timing row loaded; battle row missing

keys.moves.advancedEditor.help: These advanced fields belong only to the selected physical timing occurrence; other occurrences in the same profile are unchanged. They directly control runtime animation, motion, targeting, and projectile behavior. Projectile replacement changes this occurrence's reference to a global projectile entry; it does not edit that projectile entry itself. Paired minimum, maximum, and replacement fields are validated together.
keys.moves.playerDamage.fieldHelp: Attack {attackId} player damage. Direct per-hit damage dealt to the player by this exact Boss Attack ID. Changing it affects every listed hitbox that invokes this Attack ID, but it does not change Boss Move Power or any other Attack ID. Allowed range: {minimum}-{maximum}.
keys.moves.runtimeVariant.help: Runtime battle controls belong to the selected Normal, Plus, or Boss variant and affect every timing profile of that variant; they do not change the other variants. Timing controls are further scoped by the exact Timing Profile and Occurrence selectors below. Shared conventional Flinch is the exception: it is stored once for the base move and affects all three variants. Boss Move is variant 2; selecting it does not prove that a particular scripted boss controller uses this move.
keys.moves.bossOwners.heading: Boss Action References
keys.moves.bossOwners.help: These verified scripted boss controller profiles currently reference this Boss Move. Effective staged assignments appear after the workflow refreshes.
keys.moves.bossOwners.none: No verified scripted boss controller currently references this Boss Move. The runtime variant may still be used by another scripted encounter.

keys.moves.bossOwners.phaseModel.unverified: Controller availability has not been verified for this encounter.

keys.moves.bossOwners.bombRockDeployedContext: Context-only entries run through the separate deployed Bomb Rock choreography.
keys.moves.timingOccurrence.help: Accuracy and Cooldown are shared by every occurrence in the exact selected Timing Profile. Changing either updates all those occurrences but no other timing profile. Advanced timing fields belong only to the selected physical occurrence.
keys.moves.timingProfile.heading: Timing Profile
keys.moves.timingProfile.help: The raw timing move ID identifies one exact profile stored by the game. A runtime variant can have more than one independent timing profile. This selector scopes Accuracy, Cooldown, and the occurrence controls to that exact profile; runtime battle fields still affect every timing profile of the selected variant.
keys.moves.playerDamage.groupNote.one: Player damage is separate from Boss Move Power. The game stores it per Attack ID; this Boss Move owns {count} exact Attack row, and each Attack row can have one or more BulletParam hitboxes. Each control changes only its listed Attack ID. Values are raw player HP damage from 0 to 999, and separate rows apply only when their own hitboxes connect.
keys.moves.playerDamage.groupNote.other: Player damage is separate from Boss Move Power. The game stores it per Attack ID; this Boss Move owns {count} exact Attack rows, and each Attack row can have one or more BulletParam hitboxes. Each control changes only its listed Attack ID. Values are raw player HP damage from 0 to 999, and separate rows apply only when their own hitboxes connect.
keys.moves.playerDamage.controllerAvailabilit: The matrix shows when each verified boss controller can schedule this move. The effect-timeline cards below are independent evidence and are not assigned to a specific owner unless a direct link is verified.
No verified boss controller currently links to this Boss Move. Any available effect-timeline evidence is documented below, but no boss-specific Battle Stage or HP Phase schedule can be assigned.
keys.moves.playerDamage.status.differsFromVan: Active Bullet mapping differs from vanilla
keys.moves.playerDamage.description.withInvoc: This value modifies only Attack ID {attackId}. It removes raw player HP when one of the BulletParam hitboxes below connects; separate Attack rows are not automatically added together.
keys.moves.playerDamage.description.noInvocat: This value modifies only Attack ID {attackId}. No active BulletParam hitbox is mapped to this row, so its gameplay trigger remains unknown; separate Attack rows are not automatically added together.
keys.moves.playerDamage.role.multipleIncoming: Attack-bearing bullet with multiple incoming BulletParam links
keys.moves.playerDamage.role.noIncoming: Attack-bearing bullet with no incoming BulletParam link
keys.moves.playerDamage.localCondition.whenRe: No extra local condition: if this effect timeline reaches this exact Shoot step, it launches. This does not identify which boss controller uses the timeline.
keys.moves.playerDamage.localCondition.before: This Shoot step is enabled until the HP Phase 2 transition finishes. The boss controller still decides whether the move can be scheduled.
keys.moves.playerDamage.localCondition.afterP: This Shoot step is enabled after the HP Phase 2 transition finishes. The boss controller still decides whether the move can be scheduled.
keys.moves.playerDamage.localCondition.contro: This Shoot step runs when the boss choreography selects damage pattern {pattern}. This is a named controller branch, not an HP-phase boundary.
keys.moves.playerDamage.localCondition.identi: This Shoot step locally requires the {identity} identity or form. It does not by itself link this effect timeline to a controller schedule.
keys.moves.playerDamage.localCondition.meowst: This Shoot step runs only in Meowstic's single-projectile choreography branch. It is not an HP-phase boundary.
keys.moves.playerDamage.localCondition.unclas: This build contains a local Shoot condition that KM Editor has not classified. The exact raw tag is shown as technical detail; no phase meaning is inferred.
keys.moves.playerDamage.source.child: spawned as a child of Bullet {parentBulletId}
keys.moves.playerDamage.source.coreLanding: spawned at Bullet {parentBulletId}'s core landing impact
keys.moves.playerDamage.source.unknown: linked from Bullet {parentBulletId} by unrecognized relation {kind}
keys.moves.playerDamage.timeline.scopeFlow: Independent evidence: the owner matrix describes this move's controller schedule; the timeline cards describe exact Shoot-step conditions and BulletParam routes. No owner-to-timeline pairing is claimed unless it is directly verified.
keys.moves.playerDamage.timeline.groupHelp.on: This timeline has one exact Shoot step that can reach this damage row.
keys.moves.playerDamage.timeline.groupHelp.ot: This timeline has {count} distinct Shoot steps that can reach this damage row. They are separate local actions; their presence alone does not prove extra hits.
keys.moves.playerDamage.timeline.stepDirect: Launches Bullet {rootBulletId}, which directly invokes Attack ID {attackId}.
keys.moves.playerDamage.timeline.stepChain: Launches root Bullet {rootBulletId}. Its BulletParam route reaches Bullet {bulletId}, which invokes Attack ID {attackId}.
keys.moves.playerDamage.timeline.linkedInvoca: Bullet {bulletId} is {sources} and invokes Attack ID {attackId}.
keys.moves.playerDamage.timeline.catalogUnava: Verified vanilla timeline evidence is unavailable for this build, so the exact trigger cannot be classified.
keys.moves.playerDamage.timeline.mappingDiffe: The active Bullet mapping differs from vanilla, so the verified vanilla timeline catalog cannot establish this mapping's exact trigger.
keys.moves.playerDamage.timeline.exhaustiveNo: An exhaustive search found no effect-timeline Shoot action for Bullet {bulletId} or its BulletParam ancestors. No verified timeline launch can be assigned to this row; this does not establish its trigger or phase. The owner matrix, when present, describes only move-slot availability.

keys.profanityFilter.title: Profanity Filter Bypass
keys.profanityFilter.subtitle: Single-instruction Sword/Shield name-check bypass
keys.profanityFilter.description: Disables the in-game profanity result for player and Pokemon name entry by forcing the verified callback result to clean. It does not rewrite names, save data, word lists, or RomFS files.
keys.profanityFilter.compatibility: The bypass supports verified Sword and Shield 1.3.2 build IDs only. A game mismatch, unknown build, or unknown instruction at the owned site blocks all writes.
keys.profanityFilter.summary.unchecked: Refresh to inspect the effective exefs/main instruction and its source layer.
keys.profanityFilter.summary.installed: The KM clean-result instruction is installed at the verified game-specific site.

keys.profanityFilter.summary.notInstalled: The original game instruction is active and still calls the profanity checker.

keys.profanityFilter.summary.unsupported: The detected build ID is not a verified Sword/Shield 1.3.2 executable layout.
keys.profanityFilter.behavior.title: What the bypass changes
keys.profanityFilter.behavior.description: Forces the name-input callback's profanity result to zero, which the game treats as clean for player and Pokemon names.
keys.profanityFilter.scope.title: Exact write scope
keys.profanityFilter.scope.description: Replaces one verified 4-byte AArch64 instruction in output exefs/main. Sword and Shield use different main.text offsets.
keys.profanityFilter.preservation.title: Compatibility guard
keys.profanityFilter.preservation.description: Preserves all non-owned executable bytes and never writes Base ExeFS. Unknown bytes at the owned instruction are treated as another modification and blocked.
keys.profanityFilter.details.title: Patch details
keys.profanityFilter.details.description: The effective source is the output executable when present; otherwise KM Editor inspects the verified base executable.
keys.profanityFilter.instructionTable.title: Recognized instruction states
keys.profanityFilter.instructionTable.descrip: Only these verified instruction shapes are accepted; every other value is a conflict.
keys.profanityFilter.instructionTable.vanilla: Calls the game's profanity checker and leaves the original filter active.
keys.profanityFilter.instructionTable.kmBehav: Returns zero in w0, so the name-input callback receives a clean result.
keys.profanityFilter.instructionTable.compati: Also returns zero; reinstalling normalizes it to KM's owned instruction.
keys.profanityFilter.restore.title: Restoration behavior
keys.profanityFilter.restore.description: Restore original filter copies only the four owned bytes from verified Base ExeFS. Output exefs/main is deleted only when the complete restored file equals base; unrelated ExeFS edits are preserved.
